To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
OX40 costimulatory signals promote effector CD4 differentiation in the absence CD28, CD154, IL-12, IL-12 receptor, and T-bet.
OX40-mediated effector differentiation requires IL-2R, but not CD28, CD4, IL-12, or T-betsignaling.
OX40 costimulatory signals are required and sufficient for CD4 T cell differentiation to effector function in the absence of signals from CD28, CD4, T-bet, or IL-12R.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms by which CD4 T cells acquire effector function in vivo.
identifying the signals that regulate CD4 T cell differentiation to effector function and the role of these signals in the development of autoimmunity.
the mechanisms of T cell differentiation and the role of OX40 in regulating T cell responses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the acquisition of effector CD4 functions in response to OX40 engagement is not dependent on CD28 or CD40 costimulation or the presence of IL-12, IL-12 receptor, or T-beth, but does require IL-2 receptor signaling.
OX40 signaling is a critical and sufficient signal for CD4 T cell differentiation to effector function, but that it requires IL-2R signals for maximal differentiation to IFN-gamma secreting cells.
OX40-mediated costimulation of Ag-specific CD4 cells is not dependent on CD28, CD154, IL-12, T-bet, or IL-2R, but is dependent on IL-2.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

OX40 costimulatory signals are sufficient for differentiation to effector function and that this differentiation is independent of CD28, CD154, T-bet, and IL-12R signaling, but is dependent upon IL-2R signals.
OX40 costimulates CD4 T cell proliferation and effector function in a CD28, CD154, IL-12, and T-bet independent manner, but IL-2 signaling is required.
OX40 costimulatory signals are sufficient to drive CD4 T cell proliferation, survival, and differentiation to effector function in the absence of supporting costimulatory and differentiation signals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
OX40 signaling alone is sufficient to promote CD4 T cells to acquire effector function, and the signals provided by CD28, CD4, IL-12, IL-12 receptor, or T-bethave no effect on this process.

a single costimulation event is sufficient for driving CD4 T cells toward an effector phenotype, and that this process can be initiated without the requirement of CD28, CD28-related molecules, and T-bet.
OX40 is a potent costimulatory molecule capable of promoting differentiation to effector function in the absence of other costimulatory signals and in the absence of IL-12R or T-bet expression.
